title: Flight sim rudder pedals
description: Three-axis flight sim rudder pedals with fighter style geometry, Hall effect sensing and C++ USB HID firmware. Designed, printed, wired and programmed solo.
og_alt: Render of the flight sim rudder pedal mechanism.
lede: I fly ultralights and consumer sim pedals never felt right, so I built my own. Fighter style geometry, three axes, Hall sensors instead of potentiometers.

brief.label: Status
brief.value: In daily use at my sim

sections.label: Mechanism
paras: I designed it in SolidWorks and printed it, iterating on pivot placement and return feel.

sections.caption: The CAD assembly driven through its real linkage: yaw both ways, each toe brake, then differential braking

sections.label: Sensing
paras: Each axis uses an A1301 Hall effect sensor reading a magnet on the moving part. No contact, nothing to wear.

frames.alt: An A1301 Hall effect sensor in a TO-92 package
frames.caption: A1301 Hall sensor and magnet

sections.label: Firmware
paras: The Pro Micro shows up as a standard USB gamepad. No driver needed.

frames.caption: The Pro Micro that replaced the counterfeit Teensy

colophon: CAD animations rendered from the source assemblies. Aircraft models are third-party, illustration only.
